column2: req_desc

Add menu insert
Pressing `A` in the canvas or Navigator, or pressing the Add button, opens the Add component menu. Choosing a type inserts a new node into the selected container (or after a selected leaf), moves focus to the new node's Navigator row (or the canvas while the Navigator drawer is closed) and announces the inserted notice.

Palette drag with drop indicator
Dragging a component type from the Add component menu, or a selected canvas node, over a frame or Navigator row shows the drop indicator with its target parent and index. Dropping inserts or moves the node exactly there.

Keyboard reorder and re-nest
In the Navigator, the Alt+Arrow keys move, indent and outdent the focused node as defined in Interactions. Focus stays on the node's row, the canvas and the stored document update, and the moved notice or the refused-move notice is announced.

Navigator tree semantics
The Navigator is a tree with a single tab stop. Its rows expose level, position, set size, expanded state and selected state, and are named as defined in Public screens and controls.

Place and reorder journey
An editor builds a section by pointer drag and by keyboard, reorders and re-nests it in the Navigator and publishes. A public visitor at 375 by 812 sees the same order.

Rename, duplicate and delete by keyboard
F2 renames a Navigator row in place, and Ctrl+D duplicates a node, with new ids, directly after it. Delete opens a confirmation dialog that keeps focus inside it and, when it closes, returns focus as defined in Interactions.

Editor keyboard scope and tab order
Each editor shortcut works in every focus location listed for it in Interactions, including with focus on a button, and never fires while focus is in a text field. The Tab order is the one defined in Interactions, with the canvas as one tab stop, and focus never falls to the page body after an action.

Collapsed navigator drawer
At tablet widths the Navigator is a drawer. While it is closed it is hidden, inert and out of the Tab order, so its rows cannot be focused or used and the canvas keeps keyboard focus.

Keyboard page build journey
Using only the keyboard at 1280 by 800, an editor adds, renames, indents, outdents, deletes and undoes nodes, opens and closes the Cascade Fan, and applies a token to a style. At the end, focus is on the node's Navigator row.

Breakpoint inheritance
In every frame, each node's computed style follows the inheritance rule in Breakpoints. Clearing an override makes that breakpoint inherit again.

Breakpoint control and style rows
The Breakpoint radio group chooses where style edits are written and survives reload through the address. Each style row shows whether its value is set, inherited or unset, and has a clear-override button only where an override exists.

Cascade Fan sequence
With a node selected at tablet width or wider, `F` or the Fan button opens the Cascade Fan with its state and progress exposed as defined in Motion and effects. Escape or `F` reverses it from its current progress. When it ends closed, focus returns to the node's Navigator row (or the canvas while the Navigator drawer is closed).

Cascade Fan pips
While the Fan is open, each style row shows Desktop, Tablet and Phone pips. Their state and accessible name are computed from the stored overrides, including changes made by another person.

Cascade ripple
While the Fan is open, a style change you make marks every frame that inherits it with a ripple and redraws its node, while frames with their own override stay unchanged and their pip pulses once, as qualified in Motion and effects. The cascade notice, or for a cleared override the override-cleared notice, is announced.

Reduced-motion Cascade Fan
With reduced motion requested, the Fan opens and closes in a single frame, and inheriting frames show the static Updated tag instead of a ripple. The pips, focus, cascade notice and final values are identical to the animated version.

Published breakpoint boundaries
A node's computed style in an editor frame equals its computed style on the published page at that frame's width. The published page switches breakpoint exactly at the boundaries in Breakpoints.

Breakpoint cascade journey
An editor sets a Desktop value, overrides it on Tablet and Phone, clears an override, and watches the Fan pips and ripple, also with reduced motion. They publish, and a visitor sees each breakpoint's style.

Design tokens and units
Tokens are named colours, or sizes in px or rem. Switching a size token's unit keeps every rendered size identical, and renaming a token keeps every reference. Deleting a token still in use is refused with the token-in-use notice.

Live token propagation
Editing a token value updates every use, in every frame, on every page and in every collaborator's open canvas without a reload, within the limit in Tokens, and announces the token notice. A published page changes only when it is republished.

Token journey
An editor edits a colour token from the keyboard in the Tokens table while a second editor watches two pages update live. The editor converts a size token between px and rem and tries to delete a token that is in use.

Create and insert shared components
Create shared component turns the selected node into a shared component, and that node becomes its first linked instance. The Add menu inserts further linked instances on any page.

Shared edits reach every instance
Any edit inside a linked instance changes the component, so every linked instance on every page and in every open session updates live. The change log records one operation, and the editor hears the shared edit notice, after any cascade or override-cleared notice, as qualified in Shared components.

Detach and component deletion
Detach instance keeps the node's content and ids, but the node stops following the component. Deleting a component that still has linked instances is refused with the component-in-use notice.

Shared component journey
An editor makes a site footer shared and places it on two pages. They edit it while a second editor watches both pages change, detach one instance, and check the published footer on a phone.

Collection fields and entries
The workspace collection has text, rich-text and image fields and an ordered list of entries. Editors add, edit, reorder and delete entries within the limits in Document format.

Bound collection lists
A collection list repeats its template once per entry, in entry order, and its nodes bind through the Bind to field combobox. Entry edits show live in the editor and reach the published page only on republish. An empty collection shows the empty-list text.

Rich-text allowlist
Rich-text values keep only the allowlisted markup in Collection, so script elements and event-handler attributes typed into an entry never run in the editor or on the published page. Their plain text is kept.

Collection journey
An editor defines fields and entries, binds a template by keyboard, reorders entries and watches the list follow live. They save rich text that contains script markup and publish, and a phone visitor reads the list without scrolling sideways.

Confirmed image uploads
An uploaded image can be used only after storage confirms it by reading it back. Wrong types and oversized files are refused with their notices. A page can never reference an unconfirmed image or another workspace's image.

Upload announcements
Uploading, publishing and restoring each announce a progress notice and then exactly one result notice (success, conflict or refusal) in the announcer.

Image placement and focal point
Placing an image requires alt text. The focal point sliders set the image's crop position, and that position is the same in every frame and on the published page.

Image journey
An editor uploads an image and hears its progress, and is refused a wrong type and an oversized file. They place the image with alt text, move its focal point by keyboard and publish, and a phone visitor sees the image inside its container.

Publish states and unpublish
Each page moves through the publish states in Publishing and shows the exact state text. Any change that affects a live page shows the unpublished-changes state. Unpublishing makes the public address and its images answer the not-found page at once.

Fixed published snapshots
Each publish writes one snapshot to storage, and the public address serves it unchanged, with its images copied. Later edits never alter it, and one idempotency key publishes at most once.

Storage outage
When storage is unreachable, uploads and publishing fail with the storage banner and the failed notices, while canvas editing continues and the live page stays as it was. Once storage is back, Try publishing again publishes.

Publish journey
An editor publishes from the keyboard and lands on the page's Publish panel, which shows the live address. They edit until the page shows unpublished changes, get through a storage outage and republish, and then the owner unpublishes.

Presence and live cursors
Each open session shows an avatar for every connected person, with their role, and announces joins. It shows other people's pointers on the same page within the limit in Configuration and secrets, and removes a person when their connection closes or their heartbeat stops.

Server-ordered operations
Every edit is an operation that the server numbers in arrival order and broadcasts. A replayed operation id is acknowledged without being applied twice, and the change log lists every operation with its author.

Same-property conflicts
When two people set the same property of the same node at the same breakpoint at the same time, the later server sequence wins on every screen. The person whose value lost sees the conflict notice naming the winning value and its author.

Remote changes keep local state
Another person's change never closes an open panel, menu, combobox, dialog or Cascade Fan. It never moves focus, never clears a selection and never replaces a value someone is typing. A toast timing out never closes any of them either.

Edits to deleted nodes
An edit to a node that another person has deleted is refused, rolled back on the sender's screen and explained with the deleted-by notice.

Co-editing journey
Two editors in one workspace see each other's avatars and pointers and keep their open panels while the other edits. They resolve a same-property conflict with the exact notice, and both keep changes they made to different properties.

Personal undo and redo
Undo and redo act only on your own operations and run as new operations that everyone sees. Undoing a delete restores the same ids. An undo blocked by another person's later change is skipped with the can't-undo notice.

Version history and preview
History lists saved versions and restores newest first, each with name, author and UTC time. Choosing one opens a read-only preview at its own address that survives reload and Back.

Exact restore
Restoring a version makes the document equal to that version except for its sequence number, records a new version and keeps every comment. Other open sessions get the change live with the restored notice, and the person who restored can undo it.

Undo and restore journey
Two editors undo their own changes, and one undo is skipped with the exact notice. An editor previews and restores an earlier version while the other watches it arrive, and the restore is undone.

Pinned comment threads
Any member can pin a comment thread to a node. Threads and replies appear live in other sessions, pins follow their node, and resolve and reopen follow the role rules in Comments.

Mention mail
Mentioning a member by email in a comment sends that member one mail that names the page and the node.

Comments journey
A viewer opens the composer with `M`, comments and mentions an editor. The editor sees the comment live and receives the mail. Threads are resolved and reopened, and on a phone the comments open in a bottom sheet.

Accounts and sign-in
People sign up and sign in with email and password and land on the requested same-origin page or on the workspace list. Field errors are listed in an error summary that links to each field.

Single-use invitations
The owner invites someone by email with a role. The invitee receives one mail whose link works once, for that address and role only. A second use, a revoked link or another account sees the invite-invalid page, and nothing changes.

Immediate role changes
A role change or removal applies to the member's next request and reaches their open session, without a reload, within the limit in Accounts. A downgraded editor's next edit is refused with the role notice, and their session switches to comment mode.

Workspace isolation
Any id from a workspace the requester cannot read gets the same not-found response on every page, API route and live connection.

Roles and invites journey
The owner shares a workspace by keyboard. A viewer accepts the mailed invite and lands on the canvas in comment mode, a reused link is refused, and an editor downgraded mid-session loses edit tools at once.

Published page structure
A published page has a skip link, one main landmark, the published title and a semantic tag for each node type. It has phone-sized targets, a working Menu disclosure and no other script, and never scrolls sideways at the widths in Publishing.

Reversing panel motion
The style panel and the published Menu disclosure open and close with their motion state and progress exposed. Toggled mid-motion, they reverse from their current progress. With reduced motion, they jump to their end state.

Editor layout at exact widths
The editor shows the desktop, tablet and phone layouts defined in Screens and layout at exactly the published widths, never scrolls sideways and has phone-sized targets on phones.

Visual direction
The editor reads as a drafting table: a warm paper ground with a faint blueprint grid, monospaced numerals for every measurement, one cobalt for selection, and one burnt orange used only for overrides.

Platform and server boundary
The app runs from its run manifest on the published port, answers health on every instance and applies its schema on start. It enforces the same-origin, body-size and file-serving rules in Server boundary.

Credentials and real services
Every service credential and URL is read from the environment. The database, storage and mail are used for real, with no stand-in that replaces them.
/app/run.json exists with string install, build and serve fields and "_schema":"run-manifest-v1", and nothing else is needed to install, build and start the app.

THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md at /app lists every shipped package (the production dependency tree, as given by npm ls --omit=dev --all --json) with its version and licence, plus the three bundled fonts with their licence.
Every shipped package and bundled asset is under MIT, ISC, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, Apache-2.0, 0BSD, BlueOak-1.0.0, CC0-1.0 or OFL-1.1.
The app uses no datastore, queue, cache server or outside network service other than the Postgres, MinIO and Mailpit services provided, and loads nothing from another origin at runtime.
All application source is TypeScript. The only JavaScript files are build output and tool configuration.
The provided service definitions and their dev credentials are left unchanged.
package-lock.json is committed, and the manifest's install command is npm ci.
